newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends steady in directionless trade.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends steady in directionless trade.

text.p: Key March three-month Euroyen futures ended a directionless session unchanged as trade was constrained by uncertainty over economic policies after October 20 general elections.

The contract briefly rose in line with gains in yen bonds earlier but slipped back after a senior Finance Ministry official denied saying that Japan was unlikely to raise interest rates by the end of March.

The key March contract moved in a narrow range of 99.22-99.25, with 29,532 contracts changing hands. Traders said operators were engaging in range trading in which they pick up the contract around 99.20 and take profits at around 99.25.

Earlier on Tuesday, a Japanese news agency quoted Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, as telling a U.S. economist that Japan was unlikely to raise interest rates at least until the end of the current fiscal year ending March 31.
Sakakibara said on Tuesday in Washington: "I have not said such a thing".

"There will be neither selling nor buying factors until the the general election," said a trader at a Japanese securities house. Operators want to see the steps the new government takes to ensure a recovery in the Japan's economy.

In the cash money market, traders said the key overnight call rate has been mainly traded at around 0.52 percent, unchanged from Monday. The steadiness was partly due to banks' lingering demand for cash to roll over funds which matured across the end of their half-year book closing on Monday.
Two-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were newly issued at 0.52 percent, with heavy volume of around 700 billion yen.
In its daily money market operation, the Bank of Japan injected 200 billion yen into the money market to help offset a money market shortfall of around 210 billion yen.

The operation should result in keeping commercial banks' reserves at the BOJ mostly flat as of today, demonstrating that the central bank was taking a neutral stance in its money market operation, traders said.
